14: Loss of function (hypomorphic BubR1 insufficiency) in an oracle-confirmed BUB1B compound heterozygote (one maternal-like stop_gained allele + one paternal-like pseudokinase missense_variant in trans, entry 083). Five independent instruments plus a 3D pseudokinase pocket audit establish the mechanism: (1) Truncating stop_gained allele (entry 159): introduces a UGA premature stop codon (+4 A) in exon 17 of 23, 746 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction — canonical NMD target lacking the entire C-terminal kinase domain (aa 766-1050) with suboptimal readthrough context (R1_score=0.33; readthrough lifts WT-equivalent BubR1 by at most +1.4 percentage points vs +12.5 for doubling the missense allele). (2) Variant-effect models (entries 129, 148): score the pseudokinase missense in the top 0.47% (AlphaMissense), 2.52% (ESM1b), and 0.93% pair rank (GPN-MSA). (3) All-19,950-substitution ThermoMPNN stability atlas + 3D pseudokinase pocket audit (entries 149, 163): places the child's missense at +1.55 kcal/mol (87.3rd percentile) inside the 62-residue buried high-confidence pseudokinase hydrophobic core (RSA < 0.20, pLDDT >= 90, where 72.2% of swaps have ddG >= +1.0 kcal/mol; Boltz-2 local C-alpha RMSD = 0.45 A), matching the exact profile of published HSP90-dependent, proteasomally degraded MVA alleles (I909T, L1012P, L844F, R727C, R814H, PMID 20516114). Because the missense site is buried in an occluded non-catalytic pseudokinase (CDD cd14029, PMID 22561345), distal Lys668 deacetylation by SIRT2/NAD+ (NMN, nicotinamide, niacin, PMID 24825348) is biophysically favoured over direct active-site chaperone docking, while calibration on 8 published MVA alleles (AUROC=0.60, H083 refuted) establishes the 55%/45% prior (P(unstable)=0.55 vs P(inactive)=0.45). (4) Cross-species phenotype twin (entry 150): independently of the genome, the child's 8 HPO terms select the Bub1b^(H/H) hypomorphic mouse (~10% normal BubR1) in the top 0.99% of 76,699 MGI genotypes (p=0.026). (5) Disrupted pathway: Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC; mitotic checkpoint complex & kinetochore-microtubule attachment via B56-PP2A), causing premature chromatid separation, mosaic variegated aneuploidy, p16^(Ink4a)-mediated cellular senescence, sarcopenia (HP:0003202), growth failure, and embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (HP:0002859). No evidence supports gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity.

16:
Question. Given an oracle-confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of function in BUB1B (one stop_gained and one pseudokinase missense_variant in trans, entry 083) in a child with Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy 1, skeletal muscle atrophy (HP:0003202), and embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (HP:0002859), which therapies are scientifically justified, which drugs must be avoided, and what single experiment resolves the remaining uncertainty?

Approach. Iteration 6 (entry 163) unifies 52 candidates across Iterations 2, 4, and 5 into a four-layer, pre-registered framework. First, five independent instruments read the mechanism: 9 variant-effect models (AlphaMissense top 0.47%), a Boltz-2 fold, an all-19,950-substitution ThermoMPNN stability atlas (+1.55 kcal/mol, 87.3rd percentile, calibrated on published MVA alleles first -> prior P(unstable)=0.55 vs P(inactive)=0.45), and a match of the child's 8 HPO terms against 76,699 MGI mouse genotypes (selecting the Bub1b^(H/H) hypomorph in the top 0.99%, p=0.026). Second, we combine four generators tested against a 10,000-draw permutation null (PrimeKG walk, phenotype-twin rescues, 919-line PRISM sweep, LINCS reversal) with three mechanistic routes: R1 stop-codon readthrough across 5,837 premature stops (R1_score=0.33, contributing <=1.4% WT BubR1), R2 HCT116 drug-perturbation proteomics across 8,793 compounds, and R3 quote-verified Bub1b^(H/H) rescues and rhabdomyosarcoma trials. Third, we apply a two-source per-child safety check (PharmCAT v3.1.1 on the VCF + OnSIDES v3.1.0 HPO-matched drug labels) and a Bayesian Value-of-Information (EVPI/EVPPI/EVSI) model calibrating 1-replicate cell-line proteomics (w_R2=0.25) against in vivo mouse survival rescues (w_R1=w_R3=1.00).

Results. (1) Next measurement first: across all 20 route-weight steps, EVPI = 0.1800 is invariant, with 100% (EVPPI = 0.1800) on whether the missense allele is unstable vs inactive and 0% (0.0000) on readthrough. A single cycloheximide-chase BubR1 Western blot captures 69.1% of EVPI (EVSI = 0.1245). (2) Pre-blot & if missense_inactive (P=0.45): Dasatinib is the #1 FDA-approved candidate overall (EU=0.2537, u_inactive=0.4000, unflagged), the sole 2-generator survivor (twin|prism, 99.4th pct aneuploidy killing, p=0.0096), and the senolytic analogue of p16-clearance in Bub1b^(H/H) mice (PMID 22048312). (3) If missense_unstable (P=0.55): NMN is #1 overall (u=0.4800, restoring BubR1 via SIRT2 deacetylation in Bub1b^(H/H) mice, PMID 24825348), niacin/nicotinamide are #1 FDA-approved under calibrated R5 (u=0.1920, supported across all 3 iterations), and gliclazide/migalastat are top exploratory R2 proteomic leads (+1.47/+1.44 log2FC BubR1). (4) Presenting rhabdomyosarcoma (D4): Simvastatin/lovastatin (NCT02390843, PMID 41249736), gated on ordering a 5-gene clinical PGx panel (SLCO1B1, ABCG2, CYP2C9, G6PD, UGT1A1) because the variant-only VCF covers 1.6% (20/1,223) of PharmCAT loci. (5) Safety & Do-Not: Vincristine fails both safety arms (CYP3A5 *1/*3 + HP:0003202 muscle atrophy); RYR1 VUS flags anaesthesia risk; 33/34 Mps1/Aurora inhibitors are less effective in aneuploid lines (p=0.0096) and contraindicated.

Strengths & limitations. Pre-registered hypotheses (8 refutations reported openly), permutation nulls, VOI experimental design, executed transfer to Bloom syndrome ($0, 53 min, Jaccard 0.095). Limitations: 4-generator overlap is at chance level (p=0.263); R2 proteomics is n=1 in HCT116 (control failed, p=0.145); zero candidates have been tested in this child.
